text:
incident-bot: [P1] GPU prefill OOM surge on gpu-pool-7 — repeated container restarts detected (prefill phase). Auto-escalation: paging oncall.

sre-jake: ack, I'm on the bridge. what nodes are flapping?
oncall-maria: taking — joining now. seeing continuous restarts on pod gpu-prefill-7a/b/c in node-group ng-gpu-7.
devon-eng: logs show repeated `cudaErrorIllegalAddress` during KV cache prefill for very large contexts. example: `runtime.cc:234: cudaMemcpyAsync failed: cudaErrorIllegalAddress`
ops-lead-amy: customer-facing impact? any 5xx spikes on hosted API?
sre-jake: yes — 503 spike ~1.8% of requests over last 4m, concentrated on requests with >60k token prefill. short window customers mostly unaffected.
cust-success-oliver: flagged two paying customers on alerts: C-6132 and C-9982 — both reported degraded responses ~5m ago. prepping outreach if we confirm blast radius.
infra-kim: quick check: `kubectl get pods -n inference -o wide | grep gpu-prefill-7` shows restarts 3-7 per pod. node memory usage shows GPU memory pinned near 100% before crash.
oncall-maria: mitigation plan (short):
- apply immediate prefill-shed policy to reject/queue requests with prefill > 48k tokens
- route large-context traffic to cpu-fallback model variant (slower but stable)
- scale up hotpool on dedicated-large nodes (if available) to absorb heavy KV prefetch
- restart affected pods once policy is applied to drain bad cached state
sre-jake: +1. I'll push a temporary runtime flag: `--prefill-threshold=48000 --enable-prefill-shed=true` to the runtime fleet config for gpu-pool-7. doing dry-run on one node first.
devon-eng: rolling flag to node ng-gpu-7-01 now: `kubectl -n infra set env ds/runtime PREFILL_SHED=true PREFILL_THRESHOLD=48000` — verifying.
incident-bot: deployment event: runtime-config update applied to ng-gpu-7-01 at 03:12:14 UTC.
infra-kim: after flag: one pod on ng-gpu-7-01 accepted a large request and returned 429 for >48k token prefill (expected). subsequent GPU mem usage stayed under 92% and no restart.
ops-lead-amy: good. can we also turn on routing to smaller model? what's quick switch?
sre-jake: router rule ready — `route.prefill_long_context -> model-x-small` enabled for 10% of traffic as canary, will bump to 100% for newly identified large requests if stable.
oncall-maria: I'm going to restart the three flapping pods one-by-one after config is live. scheduling now.
devon-eng: note from logs: large context requests frequently include long system prompts + user history — some >200k tokens attempted by users with experimental ingestion. we should add request-size logging for attribution.
cust-success-oliver: starting an outbound to C-6132 and C-9982: short note that we have mitigation in progress and their requests may degrade for large-context calls; ETA to stable ~30-45m.
ops-lead-amy: decision: declare customer-impacting and create incident postmortem ticket. assigning to devon-eng and infra-kim for RCA.
incident-bot: pager rotation: oncall handoff scheduled at 04:00 UTC. oncall-maria requested takeover until then, will hand to oncall-kevin.
oncall-maria: handing to me for live mitigation. I'll own the runbook steps: prefill_shed, route-long->cpu, restart pods, observe 3x10m.
sre-jake: observed: after restarts and routing, 503 rate dropped to 0.4% and GPU restarts stopped. snapshotting metrics to SLI dashboard.
cust-success-oliver: notified customers: they acknowledged, asked for follow-up postmortem and timeline for permanent fix.
oncall-maria: temporary mitigation working. next actions:
1) develop paramized server-side limit for prefill tokens (short-term enforcement)
2) create routing policy to send oversized prefill to dedicated-highmem nodes (medium)
3) implement kernel-level guard for illegal CUDA access to avoid OOM cascade (long)
4) postmortem + customer comms (devon + infra-kim)
ops-lead-amy: please add incident severity and timeline to the comms doc and start postmortem skeleton in /docs/incidents/ (cc @devon-eng).
devon-eng: creating postmortem draft now. capturing logs: `kubectl logs -n inference pod/gpu-prefill-7a -c runtime | tail -n 200` and uploading to incident artifacts.
incident-bot: incident P1 declared: gpu-prefill-oom-nodeshift — channel renamed to #incidents and page created.
infra-kim: final check: all gpu-pool-7 nodes show GPU mem <95% and no restart events in last 12m. marking live mitigation as successful for now.
cust-success-oliver: customers updated. requesting follow-up meeting with SRE and Product for quota/rate-limit policy changes.
oncall-maria: handing off to @oncall-kevin at 04:00 UTC for overnight watch. I'll stay on-call until handoff complete. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
ops-lead-amy: great work — keep timeline and artifacts tight for postmortem.
end of thread.
